name: Pestis secunda (second European wave of plague)
summary: First major recurrence of Yersinia pestis after the 1347–53 Black Death. Chronicled as the pestis secunda or pestis puerorum because it disproportionately killed children, the post-Black-Death generation lacking adult-acquired immunity.

_quarry.structural_significance: Confirms the Black Death as a recurrent rather than singular epidemic; the demographic recovery anticipated after 1353 stalls as further waves (1369, 1374, 1390s) maintain a smaller European population through the early 15th century.
